title: The Deadline of Marseille's old port
premise: Astrid Underhill, a burned-out private security contractor in Marseille, guards clients whose secrets are worth more than their lives. When an anonymous voiceprint unlocks a dead client's encrypted server, Astrid learns the 'incident' that broke their sleep was orchestrated by the same syndicate now hunting them across three countries. To survive, Astrid must trade the server's contents—proof of a judge's corruption—to a journalist whose own loyalties are for sale. In the end, Astrid burns the archive rather than let any buyer have it, choosing justice outside every law and finally earning one unbroken night of sleep.
about_author: V. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former maritime insurance investigator who spent a decade documenting port-city underworlds before turning to fiction. They write from a rotating series of rented rooms along the Mediterranean coast.

chapters.title: The Weight of Salt Air
chapters.summary: Astrid Underhill's POV. Establishing routine: guarding a paranoid shipping magnate through Marseille's old port while insomnia gnaws. Flashback fragments of 'the incident' surface in dreams. Emotional beat: exhaustion masking hypervigilance; Astrid trusts no one, including themselves.

chapters.title: Client Number Nine
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The magnate is found drowned in his own marina pool hours after dismissing Astrid's security sweep. Police call it accidental. Astrid notices the missing hard drive and a fresh voiceprint scanner log. Beat: guilt curdling into suspicion—the job was never about protection.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Left Running
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Going through the magnate's effects, Astrid finds a scheduled task: a server in Singapore unlocks if his voiceprint is paired with a second unknown voice. Someone else has half the key. Beat: dread—the contract was bait to draw out a partner.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Sells Silence
chapters.summary: Léa Fontaine's POV, introduced: a fixer-journalist who trades in secrets, watching Astrid from a café terrace. She knows what the magnate kept and who wants it. Beat: predatory curiosity; Léa sees Astrid as either source or sacrifice.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Playing back the magnate's last voicemail to Astrid triggers the remote unlock notification. The Singapore server opens—and pings its other keyholder. Within hours, strangers are asking questions at Astrid's boarding house. Beat: invisibility shatters; the hunt begins.

chapters.title: Men Who Don't Introduce Themselves
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Two 'insurance investigators' corner Astrid in the Panier district; a chase through laundry lines and stairwells ends with Astrid escaping but leaving blood and a trail. Beat: fear sharpened into anger—these are the men from the incident.

chapters.title: The Incident, Remembered
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, full flashback. Three years ago in Genoa, Astrid's security detail failed; a protected witness died, and Astrid took the fall quietly. Now the evidence shows the failure was engineered by the syndicate to bury the witness's testimony. Beat: grief reframed as betrayal; sleep becomes impossible again.

chapters.title: An Offer on the Terrace
chapters.summary: Léa's POV. Léa approaches Astrid openly, offering the identity of the second keyholder in exchange for first publication rights. Astrid refuses; Léa lets slip a name anyway: Judge Armand Vasseur. Beat: uneasy alliance of mutual contempt and need.

chapters.title: The Judge's Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Surveillance of Vasseur reveals a magistrate laundering syndicate verdicts for years—the witness in Genoa was set to name him. The server holds recordings. Beat: cold clarity; justice through courts is a fiction Astrid once believed.

chapters.title: Singapore Calling
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The second keyholder—a disgraced forensic accountant named Wei—contacts Astrid through the server itself, terrified, offering to split the archive. Syndicate trackers close on both. Beat: fragile hope; two hunted people building trust through code.

chapters.title: Bargaining Chips
chapters.summary: Léa's POV. Léa's editor pressures her to sell Astrid's location to a syndicate broker to save her career. She stalls, torn between survival and the biggest story of her life. Beat: corruption's seduction; power offered as rescue.

chapters.title: The Safehouse That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid and Wei meet in a rented flat near the Joliette docks; it's compromised within the hour. Wei is taken; Astrid escapes with only a copied fragment of the archive. Beat: guilt rekindled—another person lost on Astrid's watch.

chapters.title: Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid confronts Léa, certain she leaked the safehouse. She didn't—but she knows who did: her own editor. Together they trace the leak to Vasseur's clerk. Beat: reluctant partnership forged in shared fury.

chapters.title: What Wei Knew
chapters.summary: Wei's POV, captive. Interrogated aboard a freighter, Wei protects the archive's true location while buying time. He leaves coded messages in his captors' own logs. Beat: quiet courage; dignity under torture.

chapters.title: The Broker's Table
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Astrid offers the syndicate a fake copy of the archive to trade for Wei, playing the mercenary they expect. The exchange is set for the old port at dawn. Beat: calculated risk; Astrid weaponizes their own reputation.

chapters.title: Dawn at the Old Port
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The exchange erupts into violence; Astrid frees Wei but is wounded, and the fake archive is exposed. Vasseur's clerk identifies Astrid to the syndicate's enforcer. Beat: chaos and cost; the plan survives by inches.

chapters.title: Every Exit Watched
chapters.summary: Léa's POV. With the city sealed by syndicate informants, Léa smuggles the wounded Astrid out via a fish-market route she's used since childhood. Her editor betrays their location anyway. Beat: loyalty tested against self-preservation; Léa chooses the story over safety.

chapters.title: The Archive Decides
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Reviewing the real archive, Astrid realizes it contains not just Vasseur's crimes but evidence implicating police, press, and the magnate himself—everyone who ever bought protection. Publishing it burns innocents too. Beat: moral vertigo; no clean hands anywhere.

chapters.title: Three Buyers, One Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Vasseur, the syndicate, and a foreign intelligence service all converge on Astrid's hiding place, each believing they've bought the archive. Astrid lets them arrive simultaneously. Beat: tension at breaking point; the trap reverses.

chapters.title: The Burning
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, climax. On a beached trawler, Astrid destroys the archive before all three buyers, broadcasting only Vasseur's confession live to the one honest prosecutor Léa found. Enforcers close in as flames rise. Beat: sacrificial resolve—justice over leverage, truth over survival.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Testimony
chapters.summary: Léa's POV. Vasseur is arrested amid public scandal; the syndicate fractures as buyers turn on each other. Léa publishes everything except Astrid's role, honoring the deal. Wei testifies from protective custody. Beat: bittersweet vindication; the system works only because someone broke it.

chapters.title: One Unbroken Night
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, resolution. Weeks later, Astrid walks the old port at dusk, unrecognized, contract-free. A stranger asks if the city is safe now. Astrid answers honestly: safer than yesterday. That night, Astrid sleeps through until morning. Beat: belonging found in letting go; rest earned, not stolen.
